speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn, I will rely on your parents' observations to guide my examination. Can you please describe the specific reason you are bringing your baby in today?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for providing that history; the lack of prenatal care and immunization records is concerning. Given the newborn's age and gender, have you noticed any jaundice, poor feeding, or a distinct "mushy" lump at the base of the skull?

REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin; REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_Diff; REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (patent ductus arteriosus), bluish non-blanching skin macules (petechiae/purpura due to thrombocytopenia), and cloudy lenses (cataracts) presents as the classic triad of congenital rubella, not cellulitis. I have already requested blood cultures and a CBC; please await the results while we confirm with serology.
